entries.title: Account abstraction, smart wallets, relayers, and paymasters on Arc: What Arc supports
entries.text:
- ERC-4337 with EntryPoint v0.7 at 0x0000000071727De22E5E9d8BAf0edAc6f37da032 (code present on both networks; the docs say to "verify before use").
- EIP-7702 set-code (type-4) transactions, from the Osaka baseline. EOAs can delegate to contract code, and paymasters can serve 7702-delegated accounts.
- EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization and receiveWithAuthorization on USDC (FiatToken v2 domain name "USDC", version "2").
- Permit2 at the canonical address. Native Stablecoin Services paymasters and multi-token gas are *planned* and not live.

entries.title: Account abstraction, smart wallets, relayers, and paymasters on Arc: Paths to gasless or sponsored transactions
entries.text:
| Path | How | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| EIP-3009 relayer | User signs typed data offchain. Your EOA calls transferWithAuthorization and pays gas in USDC. | The simplest option. ~65k gas. Bill with gasUsed*effectiveGasPrice/1e12 for 6-dp USDC. |
| ERC-4337 paymaster | Deploy a paymaster and call EntryPoint.depositTo(paymaster){value: X} | Deposit in 18-decimal native USDC: 10 USDC is 10n * 10n18n, not 10e6. Pimlico is the documented bundler for chain 5042002. Your own bundler must use maxFeePerGas ≥ 20 gwei. |
| Circle Gas Station | Circle dev-controlled SCA wallets | Auto-sponsors fees on Arc Testnet (deploy-contracts tutorial). Mainnet policy is set in the Circle Console. |
| Circle Paymaster (pay gas in USDC for 4337 accounts) | Circle product | On Arc gas is USDC anyway. Prior research found Circle's Paymaster overview omits Arc while its address page lists Arc Testnet. Treat it as unconfirmed. |
| Provider AA | Alchemy (Wallet APIs, gas sponsorship), Biconomy, Pimlico, ZeroDev, Thirdweb, Privy, Dynamic, Crossmint, Para, Turnkey, Blockradar, MetaMask Embedded Wallets, Circle Wallets | Listed on account-abstraction. The listing is not a verified deployment matrix. |

entries.title: Account abstraction, smart wallets, relayers, and paymasters on Arc: Smart-account caveats specific to Arc
entries.text:
- Memo and Multicall3From accept direct EOA callers only. A 4337 smart account, Safe, or Circle SCA or modular wallet calling them reverts (sender spoofing). Agents built on SCAs need an EOA side-wallet for memos, or must record references offchain.
- Unified Balance: SCAs (Circle Wallets SCA, Privy server wallets) can't sign spends, so use an authorized EOA delegate. SCA deposits must use allowanceStrategy: "approve", because USDC permit uses ecrecover, not ERC-1271.
- Spending policy must cover both USDC interfaces. An ERC-20 allowance, or an allowlist module scoped to ERC-20 transfer, does not stop a native-value send from the same balance. Constrain native value too, e.g. with a native-value policy module or by disallowing value calls. (Porting guide plus prior research.)

entries.title: Account abstraction, smart wallets, relayers, and paymasters on Arc: Policy-constrained agent wallets (from prior research, still relevant)

entries.text:
1. USDC is the gas token, not ETH.

3. Finality is under 1 s, so there is no need to wait for multiple confirmations.
4. Use App Kit for bridging, swaps, unified balance, onramp, and earn.

entries.title: Arc for AI agents: MCP, skills, Arc Studio, ERC-8004, ERC-8183, x402: ERC-8183: agentic commerce jobs (escrow → deliverable → settlement)
entries.text:
Testnet: AgenticCommerce reference implementation 0x0747EEf0706327138c69792bF28Cd525089e4583. No documented mainnet deployment, and the address has no code on mainnet.

Roles: client (pays), provider (does the work), evaluator (approves; in the tutorial the client doubles as evaluator). States: 0 Open → 1 Funded → 2 Submitted → 3 Completed (also 4 Rejected, 5 Expired).

| Step | Caller | Call |
|---|---|---|
| Create | client | createJob(address provider, address evaluator, uint256 expiredAt, string description, address hook) returns (uint256 jobId) (use hook = address(0) for the plain path). Emits JobCreated(jobId indexed, client indexed, provider indexed, evaluator, expiredAt, hook). |
| Price | provider | setBudget(uint256 jobId, uint256 amount, bytes optParams) (amount in USDC 6-dp units) |
| Fund | client | USDC.approve(AgenticCommerce, amount), then fund(uint256 jobId, bytes optParams) → Funded |
| Deliver | provider | submit(uint256 jobId, bytes32 deliverable, bytes optParams) (deliverable = hash of the work) → Submitted |
| Settle | evaluator | complete(uint256 jobId, bytes32 reason, bytes optParams) → Completed, escrow released to provider |
| Read | anyone | getJob(jobId) → (id, client, provider, evaluator, description, budget, expiredAt, status, hook) |

entries.title: Arc for AI agents: MCP, skills, Arc Studio, ERC-8004, ERC-8183, x402: Why Arc for agents (per the docs), plus the builder takeaway
entries.text:
| Arc property | Agent consequence |
|---|---|
| Sub-second deterministic finality | Close a job, pay, and log in one loop. No confirmation polling. |
| USDC gas (~$0.001) | The agent holds one asset. Per-invoice or per-day contractor payouts are economical. |
| Memo contract | Tie each payment to an invoice ID onchain for AP/AR reconciliation |
| Multicall3From | Payroll or batch vendor payouts in one atomic tx from the agent's EOA |
| ERC-8004/8183 | Verifiable identity, reputation, and escrowed work between agents and businesses |
| Blocklist at runtime | Pre-screen counterparties (Elliptic, TRM, Chainalysis) or the agent burns gas on reverts |
| Deterministic ordering | The docs claim ordering guarantees prevent front-running for payments |

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Send (same chain)
entries.text: Send is the simplest way for an agent to pay a vendor. For invoice reconciliation, use the raw Memo contract instead (transactions-memo-batching.md). App Kit Send has no memo field.

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Bridge (CCTP V2 burn → attest → mint)
entries.text:
- Pre-flight: const est = await kit.estimateBridge(params); est.fees // [{type:"provider", amount}, ...].
- Forwarding Service (useForwarder: true): Circle submits the destination mint, so you need no gas or wallet on the destination. The mint step's data is undefined (confirmation comes from the Iris API). A fee is deducted from the mint unless you set config.feePayment: "source", which is incompatible with custom fees.
- Default speed is FAST. Bridging out of Arc: the amount must exceed the CCTPv2 max fee (~1.4 USDC on testnet) or the burn reverts with "Max fee must be less than amount".
- Recovery guide: https://docs.arc.io/app-kit/references/bridge-error-recovery.
- Arc attestations take about 1 block (~0.5 s). Ethereum, Base, and Arbitrum as sources take 13–19 min on Standard.

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Swap (same chain or crosschain)
entries.text: Fees: 2 bps provider fee plus an optional custom fee (90/10 split with Arc). The arc-stablecoin-fx sample is built on this.

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Unified Balance (Circle Gateway under the hood)
entries.text:
- Standard deposits wait for source-chain finality (≥15 min on Ethereum L2s). Wait until totalConfirmedBalance covers the spend.
- Fast deposits (config: { transferSpeed: "FAST" } with to) use CCTP Fast plus TokenMessengerWithFees. Sources: Arbitrum, Codex, Ethereum, Ink, Linea, OP, Plume, Unichain, World Chain. Destinations: Arc, Avalanche, Polygon PoS.
- Once confirmed, spends are near-instant (Gateway docs quote under 500 ms). Fee: 0.5 bps crosschain, plus source gas per burn intent (Arc $0.0035).
- Delegates: Circle Wallets SCAs and Privy server wallets can't sign spends. Add an EOA delegate with kit.unifiedBalance.addDelegate, then depositFor and spend (see the delegate quickstart). SCA deposits need allowanceStrategy: "approve" because permit uses ecrecover, not ERC-1271.
- Trustless exit: initiateRemoveFund, then a 7-day wait, then removeFund. One pending removal per chain and address.
- Other methods: estimateDeposit, estimateSpend, getDelegateStatus, removeDelegate, setFeeRecipients, and setCustomFeePolicy.
- For a treasury agent this is the "one balance across chains" primitive the hackathon brief describes.

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Earn (vaults on Arc; USDC and EURC)
entries.text: Earn is non-custodial and runs over third-party lending vaults (Morpho is named in the fee docs). Fees come out of returns. Principal can fall in extreme conditions. It is a natural fit for the "idle treasury cash earns yield" RFB. USYC is the institutional alternative (allowlisted).

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Onramp (fiat to USDC/EURC on Arc)
entries.text: Server mints a session (valid 30 min, needs an API key) → client runs kit.onramp.fetchSession({ url: "/api/onramp/sessions", body: { appUserId, destinationAddress } }) → kit.onramp.mountIframe({ session, container, onDepositSettled }) or openWindow(...). Debit card, Apple Pay, and Google Pay need KYB in the Circle Console plus referrerDomain. Bank transfer covers select US states and the EU. No credit cards. Demo: https://onramp-demo.arc.io/. Sandbox and hosting rules (CSP, container sizing): https://docs.arc.io/app-kit/references/onramp-hosting-requirements.

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Monetization: custom fees
entries.text: 90% to you, 10% to Arc. Use a fee recipient on the source chain. Show the full breakdown before the user confirms.

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Events and observability
entries.text: kit.on("*" | action, handler) and kit.off(...). Bridge events carry { protocol: "cctp", version: "v2", traceId, values: { name, state, txHash, data, explorerUrl } }. Persist traceId and step tx hashes in your agent's audit log. Partial bridges are recoverable with retryBridge.

entries.title: App Kit (Send, Bridge, Swap, Unified Balance, Onramp, Earn): Gotchas specific to App Kit
entries.text:
- Amounts are decimal strings, not base units. Don't pass "10000000" for 10 USDC.
- On Arc, App Kit's "USDC" means the ERC-20 interface (6 dp). Your own native-balance reads are 18 dp.
- Swap needs liquidity. On Arc testnet only the USDC/EURC/cirBTC pairs exist.
- The earlier (2026-07) note that "CCTP Fast Transfer is unavailable on Arc Testnet" is superseded. Circle's table now lists Arc's Fast source as "N/A" (already fast), and App Kit defaults to FAST for inbound routes.
- The Circle Wallets adapter requires an explicit address in each from/to.

entries.title: Arc ecosystem tools and node operation: Running a node (only if you need an unmetered RPC or independent verification)
entries.text:
Anyone can run a full node (not a validator). It verifies validator signatures on each block, re-executes every transaction, and serves JSON-RPC on localhost:8545. It does not participate in consensus.

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| OS | Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+, Debian 12+). macOS works for the binaries. |
| CPU / RAM / Disk / Net | High clock speed / 64 GB+ / 1 TB+ NVMe (TLC) / 24 Mbps+ |

entries.title: Arc gas and fees: Parameters
entries.text:
| Parameter | Value |
|---|---|
| Gas unit | USDC, native, 18 decimals. 1 gwei = 1e-9 USDC. |
| Model | EIP-1559, with the per-block base fee recalculation replaced by an EWMA of block utilization |
| Base fee target | ~$0.001 per ERC-20 transfer (design target) |
| Minimum base fee | 20 gwei. maxFeePerGas below this is *silently dropped* by the mempool: no error receipt, never mined. Some RPCs return transaction underpriced. |
| Max base fee | 20,000 gwei (hard ceiling) |
| Capacity | 30M gas/block, ~60M gas/s at 0.5 s blocks |
| Base fee destination | Not burned. Base fee and tip both go to the block beneficiary. |
| Next block's base fee | Published in the parent header's extraData as 8-byte big-endian. Live: 0x00000004a817c800 = 20,000,000,000 wei = 20 gwei. |
| Priority fee | 0 is accepted and usually enough; use 1 gwei under load. eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas returns 1 wei. |

entries.title: Arc gas and fees: What things cost (at the 20 gwei floor)
entries.text:
| Action | Gas | USDC cost |
|---|---|---|
| Native USDC send | 21,000 | 21,000 × 20e9 = 4.2e14 wei = $0.00042 |
| ERC-20 transfer (~40–65k) | ~50,000 | ~$0.001 |
| EIP-3009 transferWithAuthorization | ~65,000 (docs) | ~$0.0013 |
| Contract deploy (1M gas) | 1,000,000 | $0.02 |

The hackathon slides quote "~$0.01 per transaction". The docs target ~$0.001. Both are negligible for agent use.

entries.text:
- Use type-2 (EIP-1559) or type-4 (EIP-7702) transactions. Type-3 blob txs are rejected.
- Fee RPCs: eth_gasPrice, eth_feeHistory, eth_maxPriorityFeePerGas, eth_estimateGas. The docs say values "remain accurate for a reasonable submission window" because of smoothing.
- Circle Wallets (dev-controlled) transactions take fee: { type: "level", config: { feeLevel: "MEDIUM" } }, and Circle computes the gas.

entries.title: Arc gas and fees: Recording and displaying fees in USDC
entries.text:
- Gas fees do not emit Transfer events. Derive them from receipts (gasUsed × effectiveGasPrice). Block rewards are attributed through block.miner.
- Show fees in dollars, not gwei (fee-display).
- An agent ledger should book gas as an expense line using the receipt math above. Emitter-based transfer indexing will not catch it.

entries.text:

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Money and decimals (the #1 source of bugs)
entries.text:
1. USDC is 18 decimals natively and 6 through ERC-20, with one balance. eth_getBalance, msg.value, and gas are 18 dp. USDC.balanceOf, transfer, approve, EIP-3009, and App Kit amounts are 6 dp. The raw numbers differ by 1e12. parseUnits("1", 6) sent as a native value is 1e-12 USDC. (The gas-and-fees docs example has exactly this bug.)
2. Don't show two USDC balances (native and ERC-20). They are the same money, so show one.
3. balanceOf truncates amounts below 1e-6 USDC. balanceOf == 0 does not mean empty. Book from 18-dp native values if you need exactness. Truncating when you credit under-records.
4. Gas and payments draw from the same USDC. An agent that sends its "full balance" via ERC-20 leaves nothing for gas. Keep a gas float, since ~$0.01 covers dozens of txs.
5. There is no WUSDC and no wrapping. Use 0x3600…0000 as the ERC-20. Never alias the EIP-7528 0xEeee…EEeE sentinel to it. Don't pool native against ERC-20 USDC.
6. ERC-20 allowances don't bound native sends. A contract or wallet that can send value can move USDC past any approve cap. Spending policies must cover both paths.
7. Contract USDC is the contract's native balance. SELFDESTRUCT moves it, and a native "sweep" drains ERC-20 USDC too.
8. EURC, USYC, and USDC(ERC-20) are 6 dp. cirBTC is 8 dp. WETH is 18 dp. Always call decimals().

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Transfers that revert even with enough balance (gas still spent)
entries.text:
9. Blocklist is enforced at runtime. A value transfer to or from a blocklisted address reverts, the tx is included, gas is consumed, and the receipt has status: 0. Screen counterparties first. Test with blocklisted testnet address 0x70997970C51812dc3A010C7d01b50e0d17dc79C8.
10. A value send to address(0) reverts ("Zero address not allowed"). Zero-value is fine. Burn-style patterns fail.
11. A value send to a precompile reverts. A value send to an account self-destructed earlier in the same tx reverts (Ethereum allows it).
12. SELFDESTRUCT with a balance reverts if the beneficiary is self, 0x0, blocklisted, or already destructed.
13. Always check receipt.status. Don't assume "mined = paid".

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Fees and transaction submission
entries.text:
14. maxFeePerGas < 20 gwei means the tx is silently dropped (no receipt, never mined). Floor at 20 gwei. Custom bundlers and relayers must do the same.
15. Blob (type-3) txs are rejected. Use type-2 (or type-4 for 7702).
16. The base fee is not burned (it goes to the proposer). The next base fee is in the parent extraData (8-byte BE).
17. Gas fees emit no Transfer log. Compute them from gasUsed × effectiveGasPrice (18 dp).
18. Node v0.8.0 changed error strings: insufficient balance now shows revm OutOfFunds or gas required exceeds allowance instead of insufficient funds for gas * price + value. Don't regex-match the old text.

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Blocks, time, randomness
entries.text:
19. PREVRANDAO = 0 always. Use Chainlink, Pyth, or another VRF or oracle. The EIP-4788 beacon-roots contract is absent (reads return 0x). EIP-2935 block hashes work.
20. block.timestamp is non-decreasing, not strictly increasing (1 s granularity, ~2 blocks/s). Don't use it for uniqueness or ordering. Use block number plus log index.
21. block.withdrawals is always empty. BLOBHASH returns 0 and BLOBBASEFEE returns 1.
22. Finality comes from 1 confirmation. safe and finalized tags equal latest. Don't add artificial N-confirmation waits.

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Events and indexing
entries.text:
23. Two Transfer streams. The system emitter 0xffff…FfFE (18 dp) fires for all USDC moves. 0x3600… (6 dp) fires only for ERC-20 calls. One ERC-20 transfer produces two logs. Filter by emitter or you double count. Watching only 0x3600… misses native sends.
24. On testnet, history before Zero5 used NativeCoinTransferred, NativeCoinMinted, and NativeCoinBurned from 0x1800…0000. Mainnet used EIP-7708 from genesis.
25. eth_getLogs is capped at 10,000 blocks (~85 min) on public RPCs, returning -32012. Page your queries.
26. The load-balanced public RPC can return -32014 for the head block. Retry with backoff, or query latest - 1.

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Memo, Multicall3From, and smart accounts
entries.text:
27. Memo and Multicall3From only accept direct EOA callers. SCAs, 4337 accounts, Safes, delegatecall, and staticcall revert. Circle SCA wallets and modular wallets can't use them directly.
28. Multicall3From can't forward native value (no aggregate3Value). Batch ERC-20 transfers instead.
29. Memo data is public. Store invoice hashes or IDs, not PII. Arc privacy (APS) is not live.
30. Compliance tooling must attribute calls routed through Memo and Multicall3From to the original sender.

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Tooling
entries.text:
31. Stock anvil, Hardhat network, and Tenderly-like simulators don't model Arc. Use arc-anvil --network arc or arc-forge test --fork-url.
32. viem's arcTestnet ships legacy RPCs (rpc.testnet.arc.network, which still works) and testnet.arcscan.app (redirects to explorer.testnet.arc.io). Pass http("https://rpc.testnet.arc.io") explicitly. arcTestnet needs viem ≥ 2.38. arc (mainnet) is built in too.
33. Reown AppKit needs defineChain from @reown/appkit/networks, not viem. WalletConnect prompts wallet_addEthereumChain for Arc Testnet. ConnectKit without mainnet breaks ENS lookups (CORS).
34. The explorer is Blockscout. Verify with --verifier blockscout --verifier-url https://explorer.testnet.arc.io/api/, not an Etherscan key.
35. Wallets without custom-gas-token support label USDC as "ETH".

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: App Kit, CCTP, Gateway
entries.text:
36. App Kit amounts are decimal strings ("1.00"), not base units.
37. Bridging out of Arc needs an amount > the CCTPv2 max fee (~1.4 USDC on testnet), otherwise you get Max fee must be less than amount.
38. Standard Unified Balance deposits wait for source-chain finality (≥15 min from Ethereum L2s). Use fast deposits (to Arc) or pre-fund. Only spend totalConfirmedBalance.
39. Unified Balance trustless withdrawal takes 7 days. SCAs need an EOA delegate to spend and allowanceStrategy: "approve" to deposit.
40. Swap on testnets works only on Arc Testnet, and on Arc only USDC, EURC, and cirBTC.
41. Kit keys are legacy. Use apiKey (Circle Console), which is required for Onramp and optional but rate-limited for Swap and Earn. Keys are per-environment and server-side only.
42. Circle Wallets are per-chain. Pass address in every App Kit from/to. Solana-origin crosschain transfers can't be gas-sponsored.

entries.title: Arc gotchas: sharp edges builders hit: Network status and faucet
entries.text:
43. Mainnet is live (2026-09-16), but the docs llms.txt still says "Testnet only". Arc Studio, the ERC-8004 tutorial, and the ERC-8183 tutorial are testnet-only. The ERC-8004 and ERC-8183 testnet addresses have no code on mainnet.
44. The testnet faucet (faucet.circle.com) is rate-limited. Fund one wallet, then distribute via transfers (the ERC-8183 tutorial does this). There is no mainnet faucet. Get mainnet USDC by bridging with CCTP or Gateway, or by onramp.
45. USYC requires allowlisting (a support ticket, 24–48h) even on testnet, and it is restricted to non-US institutions in production.
46. Fee parameter tables still say "may change before mainnet launch". Read eth_gasPrice live (testnet currently returns 25 gwei, mainnet 20 gwei).

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: One paragraph
entries.text: Arc is Circle's open, EVM-compatible Layer-1 "purpose-built for programmable money." USDC is the native gas token, so there is no volatile token. Finality is deterministic and sub-second: Malachite BFT under Proof-of-Authority, with blocks every ~0.48 s. Execution runs on Reth at the Osaka EVM baseline plus some Amsterdam features (EIP-7708). EURC and USYC are native at genesis. It integrates directly with Circle's platform: CCTP, Gateway, Wallets, App Kit, StableFX, and Agent Stack. Circle positions it for payments, lending, FX, treasury, and agentic commerce (arc-chain).

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Network properties
entries.text:
| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Consensus | Malachite BFT (Tendermint family), permissioned PoA validator set |
| Execution | Reth (Rust Ethereum client), EVM at the Osaka hard fork, plus EIP-7708 from Amsterdam |
| Gas token | USDC (native, 18 decimals). ERC-20 view at 0x3600…0000 (6 decimals). |
| Block time | ~0.48 s on testnet ("~2 blocks/s") |
| Finality | Deterministic, under 1 s. 1 confirmation is final. safe and finalized tags both resolve to latest. |
| Throughput (benchmarks) | 3,000+ TPS with 20 validators, under 350 ms finality. 10,000+ TPS with 4 validators. |
| Gas limit | 30M gas/block (~60M gas/s). Confirmed live: gasLimit = 30,000,000. |
| Validators | Permissioned and known institutions: SOC 2, geographically distributed, rotating proposer, uptime SLAs. The founding cohort includes BlackRock, Visa, Mastercard, and DTCC (press). |
| Developer access | Permissionless. Anyone can deploy contracts or run a (non-validating) full node. |
| Chain IDs | Mainnet 5042, testnet 5042002 |

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Two-layer architecture
entries.text:
- Consensus layer (Malachite) (consensus-layer): Propose, then Pre-vote, then Pre-commit, then Commit. Two-phase voting means two conflicting blocks can never both finalize, so there are no reorgs. It is safe with fewer than 1/3 faulty validators and live with at least 2/3 honest and online. "Optimistic responsiveness" means there are no artificial timeouts.
- Execution layer (Reth) (execution-layer) maintains state, executes the EVM, and computes the state root. Arc adds protocol-level modules:

| Module | Status | Function |
|---|---|---|
| Fee Manager | Live | USDC-denominated base fee with EWMA smoothing, targeting ~$0.001 per tx. See gas-and-fees.md. |
| CallFrom precompile | Live | Preserves the original msg.sender through Memo and Multicall3From |
| Arc Privacy Sector (APS) | Planned | Confidential Solidity execution |
| Stablecoin Services | Planned | Cross-currency settlement, paymaster-sponsored txs, multi-stablecoin gas |

Precompiles live at 0x1800…0000 through …0004 (Native Coin Authority, Native Coin Control/blocklist, System Accounting, Call From, PQ Signature Verify). See network-config.md.

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Finality: why it matters for agents
entries.text:
| Network | Finality |
|---|---|
| Arc | under 1 s, deterministic |
| Ethereum L1 | 12–15 min |
| Optimistic L2 | ~7 days (withdrawal) |

A transaction has two states only: pending or final (transaction-lifecycle). An agent can trigger downstream effects (ledger write, webhook, next payment) as soon as it has the receipt. It needs no confirmation counting, reorg rollback, or retry-on-reorg logic. Circle's CCTP and Gateway attest Arc burns after ~1 block (~0.5 s), so Arc as a source chain is fast. Other chains as source still take 13–19 min for standard attestation.

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Stablecoin-native model (the most important concept)
entries.text:
stablecoin-native-model

- One USDC balance, two interfaces:

| Interface | Decimals | Used for |
|---|---|---|
| Native (eth_getBalance, msg.value, gas) | 18 | Gas, native sends, msg.value |
| ERC-20 at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 | 6 | transfer, approve, transferFrom, allowances, permit/EIP-3009 |

- Both interfaces move the same balance. The ERC-20 balanceOf truncates the last 12 decimals, so sub-micro-USDC dust is invisible there but still exists natively. A balanceOf of 0 does not mean the native balance is 0.
- Every USDC movement emits a Transfer from the system emitter 0xffff…fffE (18 decimals, EIP-7708). ERC-20 calls also emit a 6-decimal Transfer from 0x3600…. Pick one emitter to avoid double counting.
- EURC (6 decimals) is a standard ERC-20, native at genesis and not bridged. USYC is a yield-bearing tokenized money market fund, permissioned (non-US institutions, $100k minimum). cirBTC (8 decimals) and bridged WETH (18 decimals) also exist.
- Gas launches as USDC only. Multi-stablecoin gas and protocol paymasters are "Stablecoin Services" (planned). Today, sponsor gas through ERC-4337 paymasters or Circle Gas Station. See account-abstraction-relayers-paymasters.md.

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Opt-in privacy: Arc Privacy Sector (APS), not live
entries.text:
opt-in-privacy. "Privacy features are on the roadmap and not yet available on Arc."
- Design: one chain, two execution environments (public EVM and private APS) whose state roots commit in the same block. You encrypt a normal EVM tx with the APS network public key and send it as calldata to a precompile. Validators run APS inside hardware enclaves (TEEs). Only an ack and a fixed gas cost are public. There are no public return values or logs.
- Synchronous composability between public and private contracts (atomic, no bridge).
- Default-deny isolation: per-selector policies (Open, Restricted, Locked), trust domains via addTrustee, runtime visibility enforcement, events off by default, sanitized reverts, and constant-time gas reporting.
- Cryptography: X-Wing KEM (X25519 + ML-KEM-768), HKDF-SHA256, and AES-256-GCM(-SIV); TLS 1.3 with X25519MLKEM768. The master secret key is Shamir-shared across validators and only reconstructable inside attested enclaves.
- Hackathon implication: do not promise confidential payments on Arc in a demo. Memos and all transfers are public today.

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Post-quantum security
entries.text:
post-quantum-security
- Live on mainnet: SLH-DSA-SHA2-128s verification via the precompile at 0x1800…0004. Contracts can verify PQ-signed messages as an app-layer authorization primitive, and the signer doesn't need an Arc account.
- Future: native PQ wallet signing (likely EIP-8141 frame transactions), PQ privacy (near-term, with APS), offchain infrastructure upgrades (mid-term), and PQ validator signatures (long-term).

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Roadmap items (not available yet)
entries.text:
- APS privacy, Stablecoin Services (multi-stablecoin gas and paymasters), and native PQ tx signing.
- Malachite: multi-proposer, fewer consensus rounds, and a possible move from PoA to permissioned PoS.
- Fee parameters "may be adjusted before mainnet launch". This caveat is still printed on the gas pages even though mainnet is live. Read eth_gasPrice live.

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Mainnet status (important; resolves stale info)
entries.text:
- Arc public mainnet launched 2026-09-16 (Circle press release, arc.io blog). Launch partners include Uniswap, Aave, Morpho, Chainlink, MetaMask, and Alchemy.
- Live check on 2026-09-29: rpc.mainnet.arc.io returns chain 0x13b2, block ~23.3M, and baseFeePerGas 20 gwei. Mainnet block 1 timestamp is 2026-05-15, so the chain ran privately before the public launch.
- The docs index llms.txt still says "Arc is currently available on Testnet only". That line is stale. The reference pages (connect, RPC, contract addresses) all have Mainnet tabs.
- Mainnet caveats for builders: there is no faucet ("request gas USDC through your Circle point of contact", or bridge USDC in via CCTP or Gateway). Arc Studio deploys to testnet only. The ERC-8004 and ERC-8183 docs cover testnet only. Swap works on mainnet and on Arc testnet.
- Hackathon scoring: "Mainnet > Testnet" for traction. "Real customers transacting in real USDC on mainnet count more", but test USDC counts (tameion.md).

entries.title: Arc overview and architecture: Hard forks (node-level)
entries.text: The arc-node CHANGELOG names hard forks "ZeroN". Zero5 (testnet) switched native-USDC events from the NativeCoin* events at 0x1800…0000 to EIP-7708 Transfer from 0xffff…fffE. Mainnet has used EIP-7708 since genesis. Zero7/Zero8 activated on testnet on 2026-09-03 15:00 UTC and on mainnet on 2026-09-10 15:00 UTC (v0.8.0). Zero8 charges a uniform 200-gas penalty for rejected delegatecalls into stateful Arc precompiles. v0.8.0 also changed RPC error strings for insufficient balance: eth_call and eth_estimateGas now return revm OutOfFunds text, and simple transfers return gas required exceeds allowance. Tooling that matches insufficient funds for gas * price + value must be updated (CHANGELOG).
